newsitem.title: USA: Diana plans to split into two companies.
newsitem.headline: Diana plans to split into two companies.

text.p: Diana Corp said Thursday its board of directors unanimously approved plans for a strategic restructuring that will separate the company into two publicly traded entities.
Under the restructuring plan, Diana will retain Sattel Communications Inc, which provides central office telephone and Internet switching equpment. It also will rename itself Sattel Communications.
Diana said its shares after the split will continue to trade on the New York Stock Exchange.

The restructuring plan also calls for Diana's Atlanta Provision Co Inc, C&L Communications and Valley Communications Inc to be grouped together into a newly formed company, which is expected to trade on the Nasdaq.
This company, which Diana called "NEWCO" in its release, will distribute telecommunications equipment, install and service voice and data voice networks, and distribute meat and seafood.
NEWCO shares will be a dividend to Diana holders. The distribution of the new shares will be taxable, the company said.

"This strategic restructuring is aimed at maximizing shareholder value," Richard Fisher, chairman and chief executive officer of Diana, said in a statement. "Today's announcement is the latest in a series of milestones that we set since we announced our plans to restructure The Diana Corp last June."
He added the company is on plan to complete its restructuring.
"We believe that by combining Sattel's technology with the management team we have assembled, we can provide our customers with superior products and services," Fisher said.
Diana said it is being advised by the investment banking firm of Hambrecht & Quist and the law firm of Sullivan & Cromwell.
